newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to rise, traders cautious amid Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to rise, traders cautious amid Iraq.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices would rise, tracking crude gains as tensions between Iraq and US escalates, brokers said on Tuesday.

But traders were jittery and were unwilling to quote firm bids nor offers. A local trader said bids for 180 centistoke fuel oil September barrels could remain unchanged from Monday at $109 per tonne while offers could track, crude levels and climb as high as $113.
"We would probably watch where prices were going before committing to any position," traders said.
Traders said the market is exceptionally thin today as most players were sidelined.
They said any price quotes today may not reflect actual market fundamentals as physical supplies remained adequate to meet demand.
Firm demand remained uncovered in India while pockets of enquiries were seen from China.
September paper quotes firmed by around $3 per tonne to be quoted between $112-$114.
